title: Inverse on isomorphisms with zero value elsewhere
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be any category with zero morphisms, let $X,Y$ be objects, and let $a:X\to Y$ be a morphism. Define $\operatorname{inverseOrZero}(a):Y\to X$ by classical case distinction: it is the categorical inverse of $a$ if $a$ is an isomorphism, and the zero morphism otherwise. There is no invertibility hypothesis and no property assertion; the definition is total, including on the zero morphism and in the zero category.
